prompt:
Write an accessible tabs component in TypeScript (strict mode) for React 19 and export it as

```ts
export function Tabs(props: {
  tabs: { id: string; label: string; content: React.ReactNode }[];
  defaultTabId?: string;
}): React.ReactElement
```

Markup and ARIA:
- An element with `role="tablist"` contains one `<button>` per tab with `role="tab"`, whose accessible name is the tab's `label`, in the order given.
- The selected tab has `aria-selected="true"` and `tabIndex={0}`; every other tab has `aria-selected="false"` and `tabIndex={-1}` (roving tabindex), so pressing Tab from before the component lands on the selected tab.
- Exactly one element with `role="tabpanel"` is visible at a time: it shows the selected tab's `content`. Panels of unselected tabs are either not rendered at all or carry the `hidden` attribute.
- Every tab has an `id` and an `aria-controls` equal to the `id` of its panel; the visible panel has `aria-labelledby` equal to the selected tab's `id`.
- These DOM ids must be unique in the document even when several `Tabs` with the same tab ids are rendered at once.

Behaviour:
- Initially the tab whose `id` equals `defaultTabId` is selected; without `defaultTabId`, the first tab.
- Clicking a tab selects it.
- While a tab has focus: ArrowRight selects AND focuses the next tab, wrapping from the last to the first; ArrowLeft selects and focuses the previous tab, wrapping from the first to the last; Home selects and focuses the first tab; End the last.

You may import only `react`. Answer with a single ```tsx code block containing only the module.
